EXP_DEPTH_TITLE: Deeper search buys strength - up to a point
EXP_DEPTH_TEXT:
Alpha-Beta at depth 3 is the same algorithm as its opponent and scores 48% - the expected coin flip, a good sanity check.

Each extra level of look-ahead adds strength, peaking around depth 5-7 at 64-74%.

Depth 1 (27.5%) is basically Greedy: it can't see traps two moves away.
EXP_DEPTH_NOTES: Each point is 60 games: 30 random openings, each played with both colours. With 60 games a single point carries roughly plus or minus 6 percentage points of noise, so the dip from depth 5 to 6 is within noise; the overall trend is the result. Depth 6 costs about 87 ms per move and depth 7 about 188 ms.
EXP_MCTS_TITLE: MCTS gets stronger with more simulations
EXP_MCTS_TEXT:
With 250 simulations MCTS scores just 17% - its statistics are too noisy to trust.

It overtakes Minimax at about 2,000 simulations and reaches 63-65% at 4,000-8,000.

The catch: doubling the budget doubles the thinking time, for smaller and smaller gains.
EXP_MCTS_NOTES: Same set-up: 60 games per setting against Minimax depth 3. Thinking time grows linearly: about 44 ms per move at 250 simulations, 300 ms at 2,000 and 1.2 seconds at 8,000. The tournament used 2,000.
BEST_NOTES: Alpha-Beta finished first on both boards and won every one of its twelve head-to-head matchups. In Connect 4 its closest rival was MCTS, which it beat 56% to 44%; in Connect 5 its closest rival was Minimax, which it beat 72.5% to 27.5%. It lost just 11 of 120 games in Connect 5.
